Declare a reusable measurement specification

Source: R/feature-spec.R
feature_spec.Rd

Explicit specifications use fixed ranges, independent of the canvas. Each method's definition is versioned separately from this specification's serialization format and recorded in `definitions`, so a specification states which estimator it uses whether or not that estimator was the default when it was built. Calibration is input-specific and is excluded from semantic compatibility after conversion to the target units.

Usage

feature_spec(
  properties = c("orientation", "length", "curvature", "junction_type"),
  bins = 8,
  normalize = TRUE,
  length_range = NULL,
  curvature_range = c(0, 90),
  units = c("pixels", "visual_degrees"),
  pixels_per_degree = NULL,
  estimator = c("turning", "mlv2023", "arclength"),
  curvature_scale = 1,
  branch_estimator = c("mlv2023", "arclength"),
  branch_window = 5,
  branch_power = 10,
  reference_radius = 1,
  fit_tolerance = 1,
  junction = list(),
  mat = list(),
  mapping_radius = 4,
  raster_line_width = 1,
  extraction = list()
)

Arguments

properties

Ordered feature names.

bins

Histogram bin count; junction types always use five categories.

normalize

Normalize length/count weights per 10,000 target length units.

length_range, curvature_range

Fixed increasing nonnegative bin ranges. NULL length range means c(2,400) pixels or c(0,20) visual degrees.

units

Spatial unit: pixels or degrees of visual angle. Tangent/turning angles are always measured in geometric degrees.

pixels_per_degree

Positive calibration required for visual degrees.

estimator

Contour curvature definition: vertex turning (default), published (`"mlv2023"`), or arc-length-scale curvature; see Details.

curvature_scale

Half-width of the arc-length curvature support, in target spatial units. Applies only to the arclength estimator.

branch_estimator

Published sample-based or arc-length-based scores.

branch_window

Half-window: samples for mlv2023, target spatial units for arclength.

branch_power

Positive score exponent.

reference_radius

Reference radius in target spatial units for the new separation score; published separation retains its one-pixel reference.

fit_tolerance

Straightness tolerance in target spatial units for the new branch estimator; published mirror fitting retains its one-pixel rule.

junction

Named overrides of absolute_epsilon, relative_epsilon, merge_radius, endpoint_radius, method, rule (`"exit"` or `"mlv2023"`) and gap_metric (`"euclidean"` or `"chebyshev"`; defaults to `"chebyshev"` for rule `"mlv2023"`); see [detect_junctions()]. Spatial tolerances use target units.

mat

Named overrides of threshold_angle, samples, epsilon, min_component, min_branch_points, aof (`"centered"` or `"mlv2023"`), morphology (`"minimal"`, `"hmt8"` or `"pratt"`) and branch_rule (`"invariant"` or `"mlv2023"`); see [compute_mat()]. Epsilon and component/point counts describe the raster method and remain in pixels/samples. The morphology also thins extracted contours.

mapping_radius, raster_line_width

Raster mapping distance and ink width in pixels; rasterization is explicitly a pixel-grid operation.

extraction

Named extraction settings: method, threshold, thin, min_points, simplify, provider, provider_version and lines. Simplification is in pixels. `lines` is a named list of [extract_lines()] parameters; the specification then records the line extractor's definition (`definitions["lines"]`, currently `"fdog-xdog-1"`) with every parameter filled in, the provider defaults to `"xdog_lines"`, and [trace_rgb()] passes the parameters to the backend. A provider version naming another definition of this extractor is rejected.

Value

A validated `mlv_feature_spec`. It declares methods; constructing it does not calculate features or infer extraction provenance for existing data.

Details

Curvature estimators. `"turning"` (the default) spreads each vertex's turning angle uniformly over the vertex's dual cell, the half-segments on either side of it, so every turn is counted once and a 90 degree corner integrates to 90 degrees. It has no tuning parameter, and its histograms are stable under resampling: a circle of radius 10 drawn with 16 to 128 vertices, evenly or with alternating 1:2 spacing, puts all its length in one 8-bin curvature bin, near 180/(10 pi) degrees per pixel, where `"mlv2023"` splits the unevenly sampled circles between two bins. `"arclength"` smooths the turning density with a triangular kernel of half-width `curvature_scale`, giving curvature at a stated spatial scale. `"mlv2023"` is the published MLV estimator: each segment receives the whole turn to the next segment divided by its own length, and the last segment of a contour, which has no next segment, repeats the turn from the previous one. The last vertex of every contour is therefore counted twice (the 90 degree apex of a two-segment roof integrates to 180 degrees), the closing vertex of a closed contour is not counted, and the value at a vertex depends on the length of one adjacent segment only. Use it to reproduce published values (the MLV compatibility article).
